narrative: The model estimated a 59.8% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt, meaning failure was judged more likely than passing. Because that risk was above the threshold used for admission, your law school application was rejected. The strongest factor was your Year 3 academic standing: you were in the first decile, while accepted students averaged around the sixth decile. This low standing pushed the prediction most strongly toward failure. The second most influential factor was your LSAT score of 38, slightly above the accepted-student average of 37.18; this pushed toward passing and partly offset the academic concern. Your upper-middle family income bracket was the third most influential factor and also pushed toward passing, though its effect was weaker. To improve your next application, focus first on strengthening evidence of academic readiness, especially any available Year 3 coursework, grades, or explanations for that performance. Consider retaking the LSAT only if practice tests show a meaningful gain, request feedback from the school, and apply to programs that review applicants holistically.
